claims.claim: As of 2020, Christians were the largest religious group at about 2.3 billion people, or 28.8% of the world population; Muslims were second at about 2.0 billion (25.6%); the religiously unaffiliated were third at about 1.9 billion (24.2%); Hindus about 1.2 billion (14.9%); Buddhists about 324 million (4.1%); adherents of other religions about 377 million (2.2%); and Jews about 14.8 million (0.2%).

Over 2010-2020 Muslims were the fastest-growing major religious group (an increase of about 347 million), while Buddhists were the only major group with fewer people in 2020 than a decade earlier (a decline of about 19 million).

Hinduism has no single founder; it grew out of the Vedic religious traditions of the Indian subcontinent over the second and first millennia BCE, and its foundational texts include the Vedas and Upanishads.
Buddhism traces to Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha), traditionally placed in the sixth to fifth century BCE in South Asia; its scriptures include the Tripitaka (Pali Canon).
Judaism formed among the ancient Israelites in the southern Levant during the first and second millennia BCE; its central scripture is the Hebrew Bible (Tanakh), whose first section is the Torah.
Christianity began in the first century CE in the Roman province of Judea, rooted in the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth; its scripture is the Bible (Old and New Testaments).

Islam arose in the seventh century CE on the Arabian Peninsula, associated with the Prophet Muhammad; its scripture is the Qur'an, and the migration (Hijra) from Mecca to Medina in 622 CE is a foundational event.

A universalizing religion actively invites members from any background and seeks converts across cultures (e.g., Christianity, Islam, Buddhism), while an ethnic religion is tied to a particular people, culture, or place and generally does not seek converts (e.g., Judaism, Hinduism, many folk and Indigenous religions).
Sikhism originated in the Punjab region of South Asia in the late fifteenth to early sixteenth century CE, associated with Guru Nanak (1469-1539); its scripture is the Guru Granth Sahib.

Beyond the five largest traditions, historians also name Sikhism, Jainism, Daoist and Confucian traditions of China, Indigenous and folk religions, and the growing category of the religiously unaffiliated, which does not name a single religion.

conflictingEvidence.issue: The date of the Buddha's life
positions: Traditional accounts and many textbooks place Siddhartha Gautama in the sixth century BCE
A number of modern scholars date his death somewhat later, around the early fourth century BCE
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson gives the traditional sixth-to-fifth-century-BCE placement and notes that some modern scholars date it later, presenting the range rather than a single contested exact date.

conflictingEvidence.issue: How the earliest Vedic traditions entered the Indian subcontinent
positions: Older 'Aryan invasion' framing found in some survey texts
Current scholarship favors gradual migration and complex cultural mixing rather than a single invasion
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson avoids the contested 'invasion' framing and describes Hinduism as having no single founder, emerging from Vedic traditions of the subcontinent over the second and first millennia BCE.
